THESE APPEALS COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 -4-  MFA No. 101046 of 2018  C/W MFA No. 101047 of 2018  JUDGMENT
Though matters are listed for admission, with consent of both learned counsel, they are taken up for final disposal.
Smt. Laxmavva W/O Sannamangadappa ... vs Sri. Sannamangalappa S/O Mailarappa ... on 19 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/60886109/

3 2. Challenging judgment and award dated 22.11.2017 passed by Principal Senior Civil Judge and Commissioner of Workmen's Compensation, Haveri (hereinafter referred to as 'Commissioner') in E.C.A. no.56/2014 and 57/2014, these two appeals are filed by applicants respectively.

3. Brief facts as stated are that Sri. Lingaraj @ Lingappa and Sangamesh (hereinafter referred to as 'workmen') were stated to be employed by Sannamangalappa (hereinafter referred to as 'Employer')
in his vehicle bearing registration no.KA-37/TA-5710 and TA-5711.
It was further stated that while they were on duty, on 18.1.2011, tractor trailer unit suffered accident after toppling.

In said accident,
both workmen sustained grievous injures and were admitted for treatment.
However, they did not survive.

4. Claiming compensation of their untimely death, mother of Lingaraj @ Lingappa; mother and wife of Sangamesh filed respective applications under Section 22 of Workmen's Compensation Act against employer and United India Insurance Company-insurer of tractor & trailer (herein after referred to as 'insurer').
5. On service of notice, employer entered appearance and admitted that Lingaraj and Sangamesh were employed by him on monthly salary of Rs.5,000/- and daily bhata of Rs.150/-.
He also admitted that on date of accident, they were on duty as per his instruction, but, stated that vehicle was insured with insurer and sought for dismissal of application against him.
Insurer filed objections opposing claim petition on all counts.
6. Thereafter, Commissioner framed issues and recorded evidence, wherein three witnesses were examined as PW1 to PW3.
Exs. P1
to P6 were marked.
No rebuttal evidence was led.

7. On consideration, Commissioner held that applicants had established relationship of employer and employee and that workmen died in motor accident during course of and arising out of employment and that they were earning Rs.5,000/- with Rs.100/- per day as daily bhata; applicants were entitled for compensation and insurer was liable to pay same.
It determined total compensation of Rs.5,42,275/- in E.C.A. no.56/2014 and Rs.5,27,925/- in E.C.A. no.57/2014.
Not satisfied with quantum of compensation, these appeals are filed by applicants.

8. Sri. Chandrashekhar Hosamani, learned counsel for applicants-appellants submitted that since insurer had not preferred appeal against award, relationship of employer and employee, occurrence of accident during course of and out of employment, claimants being entitled for compensation and insurer being liable to pay same are not in dispute.
9. It was submitted that claimants appeal was only on quantum insofar as monthly income of deceased.
It was submitted that claimants had stated that employer was paying Rs.5,000/- p.m. as salary, apart from Rs.150/- per day as bhata.
However, Commissioner erred in taking their monthly income at Rs.5,000/- only and therefore, sought enhancement.
10. On other hand, Sri.C.V.Angadi, learned counsel for insurer sought to support award and opposed enhancement.

It was submitted that employer had admitted that he was paying deceased Smt. Laxmavva W/O Sannamangadappa ... vs Sri. Sannamangalappa S/O Mailarappa ... on 19 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/60886109/
4
only Rs.5,000/- p.m. and therefore, no enhancement was called.
It was further submitted that during cross examination of applicants, employer had suggested that Rs.4,500/- was being paid to Lingaraj - driver and Rs.3,500/- was being paid to Sangamesh - coolie.
As Commissioner had considered higher income than said amount, there was no scope of enhancement 11.
Heard learned counsel for parties, perused impugned judgment and award.

12. From above submission, substantial question of law that arises for consideration is:
"Whether assessment of monthly income by Commissioner is contrary to evidence on record?"
13.
It is not in dispute that accident had occurred in year 2011.
Application for compensation is filed in year 2012.

Extant provision insofar as monthly wages is Section 4(1B) of Employees'
Compensation Act, 1923, which reads as follows:-
"4(1B) The Central Government may, by notification in the Official Ga zette, specify,
for the purposes of sub-section (1, such monthly wages in relation to an employee as it may consider necessary."
14.
Central Government has issued notification dated 31.05.2010 wherein income for purposes of Section 4(1B) is notified as Rs.8,000/- .
Since provision mentions that income notified by Central Government under Section 4(1B) is to be considered as monthly wages, Rs.8,000/- has to be considered as monthly income.
Therefore, substantial question of law has to be answered in affirmative as being contrary to statute.

- 10 - Consequently, compensation requires to be recomputed as follows:-
in ECA no.56/2014-Lingaraj @ Lingappa aged 24 years & factor applicable 218.47 as;
Rs.8000 X 50% X 218.47=Rs.8,73,880/; in ECA no.55/2014-Sangamesh aged 28 years - Factor applicable is 211.79 as; Rs.8000 X 50% X 211.79=Rs.8,47,160/-.
15.

Consequently, following:
ORDER i) Appeals are allowed with costs.

ii) In MFA no.101046/2018 claimants are entitled for reassessed compensation of Rs.8,73,880/- as against Rs.5,42,275/- awarded by tribunal with interest at 12% p.a.

iv) Insurer is directed to deposit balance enhanced compensation within a period six weeks from date of receipt of certified copy of this order.
